statement_token: "Let $v\\colon\\mathbb{N}\\to\\mathbb{Z}$ be the additive function defined by $v(p)=p$ for primes $p$ and $v(p^\\alpha)=p+\\alpha$ for prime powers $p^\\alpha$ with $\\alpha\\geq2$. For integers $n\\geq1$ and $b\\geq2$, call $n$ a **$v$-palindrome in base** $b$ if $b\\nmid n$, $n\\neq r_b(n)$, and $v(n)=v(r_b(n))$, where $r_b(n)$ is the integer obtained by reversing the base-$b$ digits of $n$; in base $10$, call it a $v$-palindrome. **Nonexistence conjecture for prime $v$-palindromes.** There are no prime $v$-palindromes. The claim is motivated by extensive computer calculations and complements known infinite families of composite $v$-palindromes; whether any prime examples exist remains open."
